test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-5) Official Paper (Held On: 15 June 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The angle of elevation of an aeroplane from a point on the ground is 45°. After a flight of 12 seconds horizontally, the angle of elevation changes to 30°. If the aeroplane is flying at a height of 2400 m, then find the speed of the aeroplane (in m/s).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a constant **height (h)**, the **speed** of an **aeroplane** moving horizontally is given by:

**Speed** = [**h** × (cot θ₂ − cot θ₁)] ÷ **Time**

Given: **h** = 2400 m, θ₁ = 45°, θ₂ = 30°, **Time** = 12 s.

⇒ **Speed** = [2400 × (cot 30° − cot 45°)] ÷ 12

⇒ **Speed** = 200 × (√3 − 1)

**∴ The correct answer is 200(√3 − 1) m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial **angle of elevation** (θ₁) = 45°

Final **angle of elevation** (θ₂) = 30°

**Height (h)** of the **aeroplane** = 2400 m

**Time duration (t)** = 12 seconds

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/67bf59681fa017a1d8d5dad021c10496d2591acb2cdc20677aba6e191efbc1ef.png] 

Let **x** be the horizontal distance from point **P** to the initial position and **y** be the distance to the final position.

⇒ In the first case: tan 45° = **height** ÷ **x**

⇒ 1 = 2400 ÷ **x** ⇒ **x** = 2400 m

⇒ In the second case: tan 30° = **height** ÷ **y**

⇒ 1/√3 = 2400 ÷ **y** ⇒ **y** = 2400√3 m

⇒ **Distance covered (d)** = **y** − **x** = 2400√3 − 2400 = 2400(√3 − 1) m

⇒ **Speed** = **Distance** ÷ **Time** = 2400(√3 − 1) ÷ 12

⇒ **Speed** = 200(√3 − 1) m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 200(√3 − 1) m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

The basic ratio used in height and distance is tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base. For these problems, cot θ = Base ÷ Perpendicular is also useful for horizontal distance.

Angle of Elevation and Distance

As an object moves away from the observer at a constant height, the **angle of elevation** decreases. If it moves toward the observer, the angle increases.

Speed-Distance Relation

Speed = Distance ÷ Time. In problems involving horizontal flight, the distance is the difference between horizontal components at two different time intervals.</p
